Arroyo (watercourse).fact: An arroyo (, from the Spanish arroyo (Spanish: [aˈroʝo], "brook") or wash is a dry watercourse that temporarily or seasonally fills and flows after sufficient rain. Flash floods are common in arroyos following thunderstorms.

Balancing lake.subject: Soil & Watershed
Balancing lake.question: The _____ was Element of flood management system.
Balancing lake.fact: A balancing lake (also flood basin) is a term used in the UK to describe a retention basin used to control flooding by temporarily storing flood waters.

Bank (geography).question: The _____ was Land alongside a body of water.

Bar (river morphology).subject: Soil & Watershed
Bar (river morphology).question: The _____ was Elevated region of sediment in a river that has been deposited by the flow.
Bar (river morphology).fact: A bar in a river is an elevated region of sediment (such as sand or gravel) that has been deposited by the flow. Types of bars include mid-channel bars (also called braid bars and common in braided rivers), point bars (common in meandering rivers), and mouth bars (common in river deltas).

Bayou.subject: Soil & Watershed
Bayou.question: The _____ was Body of water in flat, low-lying areas.
Bayou.fact: In usage in the Southern United States, a bayou ( ) is a body of water typically found in a flat, low-lying area. Bayous are commonly found in the Gulf Coast region of the southern United States, especially in the Mississippi River Delta, though they also exist elsewhere.

Baseflow.subject: Soil & Watershed
Baseflow.question: The _____ was Stream flow between precipitation events.
Baseflow.fact: Baseflow (also called drought flow, groundwater recession flow, low flow, low-water flow, low-water discharge and sustained or fair-weather runoff) is the portion of the streamflow that is sustained between precipitation events, fed to streams by delayed pathways.

Bed material load.subject: Soil & Watershed
Bed material load.question: The _____ was Component in the load of a river system.
Bed material load.fact: Bed material load is one of the three components included in the load of a river system the other two being: dissolved load and wash load. The bed material load is the portion of the sediment that is transported by a stream that contains material derived from the bed.

Blackwater river.question: The _____ was Slow, dark river in forested swamps or wetlands.

Boron.subject: Soil & Watershed
Boron.question: The _____ was Chemical element with atomic number 5 (B).
Boron.fact: Boron is a chemical element; it has symbol B and atomic number 5. As the lightest element of the boron group it has three valence electrons for forming covalent bonds, resulting in many compounds such as boric acid, the mineral sodium borate, and the ultra-hard crystals of boron carbide and boron nitride.

Chlorosis.subject: Soil & Watershed
Chlorosis.question: The _____ was Medical condition in plants.
Chlorosis.fact: In botany, chlorosis is a condition in which leaves produce insufficient chlorophyll. The word chlorosis is derived from the Greek khloros meaning "greenish-yellow", "pale green", "pale", "pallid", or "fresh".

Chronic condition.subject: Soil & Watershed
Chronic condition.question: The _____ was Persistent human health condition or disease.
Chronic condition.fact: A chronic condition, also called a chronic disease or chronic illness, is a health condition or disease that is persistent or otherwise long-lasting in its effects.

Community (ecology).subject: Soil & Watershed
Community (ecology).question: The _____ was Associated populations of species in a given area.
Community (ecology).fact: In ecology, a community is a group or association of populations of multiple species occupying the same geographical area at the same time, also called a biocoenosis, biotic community, biological community, ecological community, or life assemblage. The term community has a variety of uses.

Consumer (food chain).subject: Soil & Watershed
Consumer (food chain).question: The _____ was Living creatures that eat organisms from a different population.
Consumer (food chain).fact: A consumer in a food chain is a living creature that eats organisms from a different population. A consumer is a heterotroph and a producer is an autotroph.

Cytochrome.subject: Soil & Watershed
Cytochrome.question: The _____ was Redox-active proteins containing a heme with a Fe atom as a cofactor.
Cytochrome.fact: Cytochromes are redox-active proteins containing a heme, with a central iron (Fe) atom at its core, as a cofactor. Four varieties are recognized by the International Union of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology (IUBMB), cytochromes a, cytochromes b, cytochromes c and cytochrome d.

Cytochrome c oxidase.subject: Soil & Watershed
Cytochrome c oxidase.question: The _____ was Aerobic respiration enzyme.
Cytochrome c oxidase.fact: The enzyme cytochrome c oxidase or Complex IV (was EC 1.9.3.1, now reclassified as a translocase EC 7.1.1.9) is a large transmembrane protein complex found in bacteria, archaea, and the mitochondria of eukaryotes, including humans.

Deforestation.subject: Soil & Watershed
Deforestation.question: The _____ was Conversion of forest to non-forest for human use.
Deforestation.fact: Deforestation or forest clearance is the removal and destruction of a forest or stand of trees from land that is then converted to non-forest use. Deforestation can involve conversion of forest land to farms, ranches, or urban use.

Deforestation.subject: Soil & Watershed
Deforestation.question: In _____, nearly a third of the overall tree cover loss, or 3.8 million hectares, occurred within humid tropical primary forests

Deforestation.subject: Soil & Watershed
Deforestation.question: In _____ nearly 90% of global deforestation was caused by agriculture, with cropland expansion and pasture creation the primary drivers, this is up from more than 80% in 2012

Deposition (geology).subject: Soil & Watershed
Deposition (geology).question: The _____ was Natural addition of materials to a landmass.
Deposition (geology).fact: Deposition is the geological process in which sediments, soil and rocks are added to a landform or landmass. Wind, ice, water, and gravity transport previously weathered surface material, which, at the loss of enough kinetic energy in the fluid, is deposited, building up layers of sediment.

Fluvial sediment processes.subject: Soil & Watershed
Fluvial sediment processes.question: The _____ was Sediment processes associated with rivers and streams.
Fluvial sediment processes.fact: In geography and geology, fluvial sediment processes or fluvial sediment transport are associated with rivers and streams and the deposits and landforms created by sediments.

Eutrophication.subject: Soil & Watershed
Eutrophication.question: The _____ was Accumulation of nutrients in water.
Eutrophication.fact: Eutrophication is a general term describing a process in which nutrients accumulate in a body of water, resulting in an increased growth of organisms that may deplete the oxygen in the water; i.e. Eutrophication may occur naturally or as a result of human actions.

Food energy.subject: Soil & Watershed
Food energy.question: The _____ was Chemical energy animals derive from food.
Food energy.fact: Food energy is chemical energy that animals derive from food to sustain their metabolism and muscular activity.

Harmful algal bloom.subject: Soil & Watershed
Harmful algal bloom.question: The _____ was Population explosion of organisms that can kill marine life.
Harmful algal bloom.fact: A harmful algal bloom (HAB), or excessive algae growth, sometimes called a red tide in marine environments, is an algal bloom that causes negative impacts to other organisms by production of natural algae-produced toxins, water deoxygenation, mechanical damage to other organisms, or by other means.

Aerial firefighting.subject: Soil & Watershed
Aerial firefighting.question: The _____ was Use of aircraft to combat wildfires.
Aerial firefighting.fact: Aerial firefighting, also called waterbombing, is the use of aircraft and other aerial resources to combat wildfires.

Afforestation in Japan.subject: Soil & Watershed
Afforestation in Japan.question: The _____ was Projects to plant native tree species in open areas.
Afforestation in Japan.fact: The Japanese temperate rainforest is well sustained and maintains a high biodiversity. One method that has been utilized in maintaining the health of forests in Japan has been afforestation.

Afforestation in Scotland.subject: Soil & Watershed
Afforestation in Scotland.question: The _____ was Scotland's environment.
Afforestation in Scotland.fact: Afforestation efforts in Scotland have provided an increase in woodland expansion. By the 20th century mark, Scotland had diminished woodland coverage to 5% of Scotland's land area.

Afforestation in Scotland.question: The Scottish government released their Draft Climate Change Plan in January _____

Afforestation in Scotland.question: In _____ the Thatcher government amended the 1967 Forestry Act that included a shift in favor of privatization of woodland expansion
Afforestation in Scotland.fact: In 1981 the Thatcher government amended the 1967 Forestry Act that included a shift in favor of privatization of woodland expansion.

Angle gauge.subject: Soil & Watershed
Angle gauge.question: The _____ was Tool used by foresters.
Angle gauge.fact: An angle gauge is a tool used by foresters to determine which trees to measure when using a variable radius plot design in forest inventory. An angle gauge is similar to a wedge prism though it must be held a fixed distance from the eye to work properly.

Anna Trugman.subject: Soil & Watershed

Anna Trugman.fact: Anna Trugman is an associate professor at the University of California, Santa Barbara who is known for her work modeling the consumption of carbon dioxide by terrestrial ecosystems.
